newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends sluggish session mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends sluggish session mostly higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mainly higher on Monday, bolstered by commission house buying, traders said.
However, interest in the market was fairly light, with the London market still closed on Monday for the Easter holiday, they added. LIFFE reopens on Tuesday.
May futures closed up 1.35 cents per lb, to 191.15 cents, after ranging from 193.50 to 187.80. Second-position July rose 1.60 cents, to 174.15, while the back months finished up 1.00 to down 2.50.
The May/July switch narrowed slightly to 17.00 cents, from 17.25 cents at the close on Thursday.
The market headed higher at the outset, as a combination of trade and speculative buying touched off light buy-stops above last Thursday's high of 192.00, dealers said.
But a round of long liquidation by locals and light profit-taking cut into early gains and prevented a test of key technical resistance at 195.00 cents in the May contract.

Some dealers said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data, which showed non-commercial net long positions down to 5,307 lots as of March 25 compared with some 9,000 lots net non-commercial longs two weeks ago, was supportive.
"The CFTC report was fairly positive," one trader said. "I think it shows that the funds still have some more ammunition."
On the charts, traders said a finish today above 191.00 cents basis May was viewed as constructive and could lead to a test of 195.00-196.00 in the near-term.
On the downside, support was seen at 187.00 cents, with stronger support noted at 185.00 cents.
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged at 83,578 60-kg bags as of March 27. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume was light at an estimated 6,371 lots, down from Thursday's official tally of 12,907 lots.
